hints: The root splits inorder into left and right subtree segments.
Reconstruct the two segments and output the root after both subtrees.
analogy: The inorder sequence separates the two branches, while preorder identifies the next branch root.
example: Preorder [2,1,3] and inorder [1,2,3] describe root 2 with children 1 and 3, so postorder is [1,3,2].
algorithm: Map every label to its inorder index. For each subtree, take the first preorder element as root, use its inorder position to obtain the left subtree size, and process the left and right preorder segments before outputting the root. Use an explicit stack to avoid recursion overflow on a chain.
correctness: Distinct labels uniquely locate each root in inorder, dividing exactly its left and right descendants. Inductively processing these segments before the root produces their postorder followed by the root.
complexity: For n vertices, O(n) time and O(n) space.
